guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Collapse progressively discloses long or secondary content behind a clickable header - the content stays hidden until expanded, keeping the page compact while still making the detail available on demand. When to Use An FAQ list - each question collapsed until clicked. Settings section grouping or filter panel sections - organizing a long settings page into expandable chunks. An order details breakdown or terms and conditions section - long content that most users won't need expanded by default. When Not to Use Content everyone needs to see immediately - hiding essential information behind a click adds friction; show it directly instead. A single, always-visible section with no reason to hide it - a static Card or plain section is simpler when there's no benefit to collapsing. Switching between different views of content rather than showing/hiding one section - use Tabs instead of Collapse. Best Practices Make the whole header row clickable, not just a small chevron icon, so the hit target is generous. Default the most commonly needed section open when there's a clear default, rather than collapsing everything. Animate the expand/collapse transition smoothly so content doesn't just snap in and out abruptly. Do and Don't Do Shipping detailsDelivered by courier, 2-4 business days. A header naming exactly what is inside, so opening it is a deliberate choice rather than a guess. Don't More infoDetails Two panels both titled something generic give the user no way to predict which one holds what they need - they have to open both. Accessibility The header exposes aria-expanded, reflecting whether its panel is currently open. The header is a real, keyboard-operable button, not a div with only a click handler. The expanded panel is programmatically associated with its header via aria-controls, so the relationship is explicit.
